about: The Collect seeks help through the merits of Antoninus, God’s confessor and bishop. Proclaiming God wondrous in Antoninus, it asks that we may glory in His mercy toward us.

seg.tr: Lord, may we be helped by the merits of Saint Antoninus, Your confessor and bishop, so that, just as we proclaim You wondrous in him, so we may glory that You have been merciful toward us. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, Your Son, who lives and reigns with You in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God, forever and ever.

a.g: we proclaim You wondrous in him
we may glory that You have been merciful toward us
who lives and reigns with You

ex.w002: This is Antoninus, named as confessor and bishop in the source heading, not Anthony of Padua.
ex.w004: Here “confessor” is a saint’s title: one who confessed the faith, not a priest hearing a confession in this sentence.
ex.w007: The saint’s title here means bishop. It does not identify him as pope.
ex.w015: “Wondrous” describes God, whom the prayer proclaims wondrous in Antoninus.
ex.w021: “Have been” presents God’s mercy as preceding the glorying for which the prayer asks. The understood subject is “You.”
ex.w039: “God” refers to the Son, who lives and reigns with the Father in the unity of the Holy Spirit.
